title: Add Operational Safe Mode and Stage-based Rollback Criteria to PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: A recent KV cache stall incident uncovered gaps between postmortem actions and the product requirements that ship the runtime. This ticket captures PRD updates to explicitly require an "operational safe mode" (a reduced-function serving path the platform can enter automatically) and stage-based rollback criteria tied to observable SLO breaches. The goal is to convert postmortem action items into concrete acceptance criteria, owner responsibilities, and release gating in the PRD for runtime and console changes.

This PRD fragment augments the existing runtime-1.x requirements: it defines the safe-mode behavior, entry/exit signals, allowed feature set in safe mode, telemetry needs, and the automation and human-operator steps required to enact staged rollbacks and emergency re-route policies. It includes verification steps, synthetic checks, and a small opt-in migration plan for Dedicated customers.

Scope: Include hosted API and Dedicated runtime; do not include Private on-prem packaging in this ticket (separate follow-up). Backfill runbook steps and link to postmortem artifact PM-POST-2025-11-kv-stall.
acceptance_criteria: Safe mode is specified in the PRD: definition, allowed endpoints, and traffic shaping rules are included in a single PRD section.
Automated entry: A documented set of metrics and thresholds (tail latency p95/p99, sustained error rate, KV cache miss regen rate) that trigger safe mode; thresholds are numeric and verifiable.
Automated exit: Clear cooldown and verification window with synthetic traffic tests to validate healing before normal routing resumes.
Rollback stages are defined: Canary rollback (10% traffic), Partial rollback (50% traffic), Full rollback (100% traffic) with exact SLO breach triggers and escalation steps.
Runbook tasks are itemized and owned: operator steps, GitHub PR links for engineered rollbacks, and diagnostics checklist for triage are present.
Synthetic verification: Canary smoke tests and tail-latency-focused synthetic traffic are added to CI/CD gating for runtime-1.18 branch with pass/fail criteria.
Telemetry: Dashboards and alert rules for the safe-mode entry signals, plus a cost/latency tag for rollback events, are specified and mapped to console dashboards and notification channels.
Privacy & compliance note: For Dedicated customers, the opt-in migration plan and tenant isolation implications are documented (no secrets exposure during rollback procedures).

Acceptance tests: A documented test plan that can be executed in staging to simulate the postmortem scenario (KV rehydration stall) and demonstrate safe-mode entry, rollback staging, and recovery within SLOs.
scope_changes: Add safe mode behavioral spec to runtime PRD (new section) covering hosted and Dedicated runtime only.
Increase telemetry retention for safe-mode related traces from 7 days to 30 days for initial rollout for debugging (temporary change; revisit after 90 days).
Include canary synthetic tests in the release gating for runtime-1.18; disallow merge to main without green synthetic run for the canary path.
Exclude on-prem/private full automation in this iteration; document required manual steps and create a follow-up ticket for Private automation.
decisions: Adopt a three-stage rollback model (10/50/100) aligned to cost and customer impact trade-offs after cross-functional review.
Use existing KV cache regen metrics (kv_cache_miss_rate, kv_rehydrate_latency, kv_rehydrate_errors) as primary safe-mode signals to avoid instrumentation churn.
Temporary telemetry retention bump approved for debugging; product and infra will re-evaluate cost after initial 90-day window.
Operational Safe Mode will intentionally restrict model variants that require KV cache priming — the runtime will prefer stateless model variants when in safe mode.
